subject: Clarify: Key rotation proof + sample evidence packet for SIG submission
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@northbridge.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <m.ruiz@northbridge.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: SIG packet: key rotation evidence and redaction approach

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our SIG submission we need a compact evidence packet that proves Redwood's key rotation practices and that the logs we receive for validation are already redacted to remove customer PII. Specifically Northbridge needs: 

- A short sample of KMS rotation logs showing an automated rotation event (timestamps + key IDs)
- An explanation of HSM usage vs software KMS for model encryption keys
- A one-page redaction guidance doc that shows what fields are removed from telemetry we pull for audits

Can you confirm whether you can provide a sample (sanitized) rotation log and the redaction guidance by next Tuesday (2027-04-27)? If not, what is the earliest date? We're coordinating with procurement to finalize the SIG by end of the month.

Also please call out any controls mapped to CC6 and CC7 (SOC 2) and which ISO 27001 clauses you align to for key management.

Appreciate it—
Liam

--
Liam O'Neill
Head of Security, Northbridge Analytics
liam.oneill@northbridge.com
+1 415-555-0142

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@northbridge.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <m.ruiz@northbridge.com>; Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-23T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG packet: key rotation evidence and redaction approach

Hi Liam—

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide a sanitized sample rotation log and a redaction guidance page. High-level answers inline, and I added Kimberly (Security Ops) to help with the artifact handoff. Priyo (copying separately) will help map the specific SIG controls.

- Sample rotation logs: we will provide a zipped sample (kms-rotation-sample-logs.zip) containing 3 sanitized events spanning a 90-day window. Each entry will include: rotation_time (UTC), key_id (hashed), initiating_service (redacted service name), and rotation_result.
- HSM vs software KMS: Redwood uses a cloud KMS for routine workload keys and a customer-seeded HSM-backed key for signing of long-lived root material when customers opt into dedicated/private. We'll include a short schematic and statement of how private deployments change key custody.
- Redaction guidance: attached as redaction-guidelines.pdf; it enumerates fields removed from telemetry, the regex patterns we apply, and the manual review gating for ambiguous tokens.

Control mapping: Kimberly will attach the SIG control mapping workbook (sig-control-mapping.xlsx) with CC6/CC7 crosswalks to our SOC 2 and ISO statements. Expect the initial packet by EOD 2027-04-24; final sanitized zip by 2027-04-26.

Questions: 
1) For the logs, do you prefer rotation_time in UTC ISO or epoch? We will default to ISO with timezone.
2) Will Northbridge require notarized signatures / witnessed attestations for any of these artifacts?

Best,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Manager, Trust & Security Programs
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@northbridge.com>; Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-24T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG packet: key rotation evidence and redaction approach

Hi Liam — quick notes from Security Ops and attached workbook draft.

Attached: sig-control-mapping.xlsx (tabbed: SOC2_CC6_CC7; ISO27001_KMS; EvidenceIndex)

Summary:
- SOC 2 CC6 (Logical & Physical Access Controls): we map rotation and key custody controls to CC6.3 and CC6.4 via automated rotation, MFA for key ops, and HSM-backed key signing for private customers.
- SOC 2 CC7 (Change Management): our rotation pipeline is driven by IaC and pipeline changes are covered by PR review + signed deploys; the workbook shows ticket IDs and sample PRs as references (redacted).
- ISO 27001: key management aligns to A.8 (asset management) and A.10 (cryptography); the ISO tab lists clause numbers and sample evidence locations.

Sanitization approach for logs:
- We hash any key identifiers presented to external auditors with salted SHA256 and replace service-hostnames with a deterministic token (SERVICE_01).
- We redact any user/email fields; telemetry fields that may contain PII go through regex-based scrub then manual review.

Delivery plan:
- 2027-04-24 EOD: Draft workbook + redaction guidance (PDF) sent to your Drive link
- 2027-04-26 EOD: Zipped sample logs (sanitized) + brief README describing fields

If that cadence works, we will upload to the shared drive and grant NB security team read-only access.

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Security Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@northbridge.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>; Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <m.ruiz@northbridge.com>; Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG packet: key rotation evidence and redaction approach

Thanks Irene/Kimberly — that schedule works. A couple of quick clarifications before you pack the artifacts: 

- For the sample log please include one event that shows a key rotation triggered by a scheduled rotation policy (automated) and one that shows a manual rotation (operator-initiated) so our reviewers can see both flows.
- On the HSM statement: we only need confirmation that root key material can be generated/managed with HSM-backed protection for private deployments; no need for production HSM audit reports. A vendor statement is fine.
- For redaction: please include the regex rules as plain text in the PDF (we will not request raw logs beyond the zipped sample).

When you upload, please add the Drive link to the evidence index tab in the workbook and ping us for access. Once we have the artifacts the procurement team will complete the SIG review and get the RFP to legal for signature.

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Liam

--
Liam O'Neill
Head of Security, Northbridge Analytics
liam.oneill@northbridge.com
